description.en: A small living Isotelus reconstruction with a broad low shield, eight thoracic segments and similarly sized head and tail shields. Ventral limbs, thickness, colour and posture are inferred rather than preserved soft tissues of the anchor specimen.
description.zh: 小型Isotelus活体复原，具有宽低背甲、八节胸部及大小相近的头尾盾。腹肢、体厚、颜色与姿态为推断，并非主锚标本保存的软组织。

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Complete conservative living reconstruction anchored to PRI76285, approximately 30 mm body: broad low oval dorsal shield, eight thoracic segments, large approximately balanced head and tail shields. Not a fossil slab.

scientific_limits.en: Museum specimen length is approximately 30 mm excluding rock. Other proportions are estimates from an oblique scan preview, not orthographic measurements. Ventral limbs are inferred and not preserved in this reference. Small I. gigas can retain genal spines; do not impose the large-adult spineless condition or long spines from other Isotelus species. Exact ventral limb count, thickness, color and posture remain uncertain.
scientific_limits.zh: 馆藏本体约30毫米，不含岩石；其他比例由斜视扫描预览估计，非正投影实测。腹肢为推定，不是该标本保存的软组织。小型I.gigas可能保留颊刺，不套用大型成体无刺定式，也不借其他种的长刺；精确腹肢数、厚度、颜色及姿态仍不确定。

scale.uncertainty: Approximate specimen length from PRI. Other dimensions are restrained construction estimates, about 20 percent uncertainty, not separate specimen measurements.

anatomy: Broad low oval shield; large subtriangular/parabolic head and similar-sized smooth pygidium. Keep head, eight-segment thorax and tail each approximately one third of body length.
Broad central axis and eight free thoracic tergites; restrained pleural furrows and rounded short lateral ends. Do not copy the thirteen ribs and tiny tail of Elrathia.
Paired prominent raised eyes on the head, fused/weakly delimited glabella; smooth-looking surface at model scale with shallow pits optional, not pronounced tubercles.

Small restrained genal points permissible at this small size, maximum approximately 2 mm as inference; no long spines extending down most of the thorax. PRI preview is insufficient to determine fine genal tips.
Large subtriangular tail shield with weak axial indication, not a tiny rounded tail or a fan of long spines. Twelve faint axial rings described for species need not be rendered as deep grooves.

Slender paired antennae and three postantennal cephalic limb pairs conservatively restored. Keep first postantennal pair smaller near hypostome, reflecting tentative published Isotelus differentiation, not asserted specimen proof.
Eight thoracic paired biramous limbs, one pair under each tergite. Walking branches under pleurae and small outer filament branches, no dorsal gills.

Twelve progressively smaller paired pygidial limbs are an explicitly inferred visualization convention, not a measured PRI count and not proof of one-to-one correspondence with dorsal axial rings. Keep them shallow and beneath the broad tail, attached along axial region.
Complete low walking animal with restrained ventral clearance, no rock, no fossil labels. Color and posture artistic.
restoration_boundaries: PRI76285 is the sole body size and primary dorsal silhouette anchor; no larger species or slab measurements.
Harvard species account supports eight segments, raised eyes, subtriangular shields, weak twelve axial rings and size-dependent genal spines; no claim its photographed specimens are PRI76285.

Hegna and Briggs 2011 is a primary abstract on rare Isotelus ventral remains. Differentiated smaller cephalic limb pair is tentative and pygidial tissue restricted toward axis; precise PRI ventral anatomy unknown.
Ventral limb counts and branch details remain conservative trilobite reconstruction, not a scan of soft parts. Any rings do not independently prove appendage counts.
